plants.description: Upright violet spires on near-black stems. Cut back after the first flush for a second show.
Deep purple flowers for months on end. Mulch over winter in colder gardens.
plants.notes: Borderline hardy in colder areas; lift or mulch heavily in winter.

plants.description: Violet-blue saucers from June to the first frosts. Weaves between neighbours.
Aromatic, weed-smothering carpet with soft pink flowers. Copes with dry shade.
Soft lavender-blue haze with grey, aromatic leaves. A bee favourite.
Apricot flowers held on wiry stems above a neat clump of leaves.
Crimson pincushions that float and weave through neighbouring plants.
Tall, see-through stems topped with purple clusters. Self-seeds gently.
Pink daisies with copper cones. Leave seedheads standing for winter birds.
Creamy white daisies with an orange-brown centre. Loved by butterflies.
Flat heads that open rust-orange and fade to soft apricot.
Pale lemon flower plates over feathery silver leaves.
Papery, pincushion flowers in soft pink. Good for cutting.
Golden daisies with dark centres that carry the border into autumn.
Coppery-red daisies that fade to burnt orange. Needs reliable moisture.
Slender crimson tapers above a leafy mound, flowering for months.
Pure white flowers on tall stems from late summer. Spreads slowly.
Rose-pink flowers on wiry stems in late summer and autumn.
Fleshy leaves and flat heads that turn from pink to russet. Good winter outline.
Dense smoky-violet spikes with aniseed-scented leaves. Hates winter wet.
plants.notes: Hardy to cold but rots in wet winter soil.

plants.description: Airy wands of white flowers that dance in the breeze. Needs good drainage.
Steely-blue thistle-like heads on branching stems. Thrives on neglect.
Silver stems and a haze of lavender-blue. Cut back hard in spring.
Compact, scented and evergreen. Trim after flowering to keep it tidy.
A cloud of tiny lilac flowers above fine, fern-like leaves.
Small claret bobbles on wiry, see-through stems.
Tall white candles on whorled stems. Strong architecture that needs no staking.
A big, late statement with domed dusky-pink heads. Butterflies flock to it.
Classic large white daisies. Deadhead to keep it flowering.
Scarlet trumpets with a yellow throat above arching leaves.
Arching sprays of flame-red flowers over sword-shaped leaves.
A mass of small violet-blue daisies in early autumn. Mildew-resistant.
Lavender-blue daisies for a remarkably long season.
Wine-red tubular flowers all summer. Leave old stems until spring.
Tiny white-and-pink daisies spilling over edges for months.
Elegant blue flowers in late spring, then upright grassy leaves.
Purple drumsticks in May, planted as bulbs in autumn between perennials.
White spires with maroon-speckled throats. Short-lived but self-seeds.
Large creamy plumes above bold leaves. Ideal for the back of a shady border.
Soft yellow whorls on stiff stems; the seedheads stand all winter.
Lacy white umbels like a refined cow parsley. Hoverflies love it.
Evergreen blue-grey columns with huge lime heads in spring. Sap irritates skin.
Neat domes of acid-yellow in spring, turning red in autumn.
Velvety leaves that hold raindrops, with froths of lime-green flowers.
Glossy bronze-purple leaves all year round; small white flower sprays.
Silver-frosted heart-shaped leaves with forget-me-not flowers.
Gentian-blue flowers in early spring, an important early bee plant.
Nodding flowers in late winter. Remove old leaves in January.
Delicate yellow spring flowers over heart-shaped, bronze-tinted leaves.
Huge golden oat-like heads on see-through stems; a focal point that catches the light.
Soft, blonde ponytails that move in every breeze. Comb out old growth in spring.
Bolt-upright buff plumes that stand from June right through winter.
A screen of fine, see-through flower stems that turn gold in autumn.
Clouds of tiny golden flowers above a neat evergreen tuft.
Lime-green tufts topped with silvery spikes in late summer. A tidy edging grass.
Cascading bright green blades that flow like water. Slow to establish.
Evergreen cream-and-green striped tufts that brighten dark corners.
Tough native fern with shuttlecocks of upright fronds. Copes with dry shade.
Evergreen, finely divided fronds with a soft, mossy texture.
Bronze buds opening to soft apricot and cream pokers from midsummer.
Slim spires of small rust-amber bells. Short-lived but seeds gently.
Flame-orange heads in early summer on red-ribbed stems. Spreads by runners.
Vivid magenta flowers with a black eye, scrambling through neighbours.
Brick-orange flower plates with yellow eyes over grey, feathery foliage.
